non_blocking_findings.summary: The corrected C1 check cannot see a body pose applied at the safety site. It checks that every in-call refresh line applied nothing and that the scan age did not change. But the timer sites log a body pose only when the body age before the refresh exceeds 0.05 s, and C1 re-stamps the body pose, so its age is 0. The cell's claim, 'nothing applied', holds only through green C1's map digest being equal to red's. I verified that equality in all four states; analyze.py does not assert it. Likewise, C4's 'no stale signature' tests only two signature classes: a conflict stop at 0.000 s and a whole-route block. The other classes appear in no green C4 or C6 call either.

The green C4/C6 call sections have 0 lines matching remaining_spline_invalid, final_spline_rejected, inside an obstacle or terminal point.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: In a later contract: assert that green C1's digest and recheck equal red's, and extend the C4/C6 no-stale check to remaining_spline_invalid, final_spline_rejected and 'inside an obstacle'.

non_blocking_findings.summary: Several records overstate or misstate small points. (a) COMPONENT_RESULTS.md gives the 0.30 s later start and the newer scans as the reason green C4 succeeds at the corridor entry, but nothing isolates either as the cause. The diagnosis's failure at Δ = 0 was WrongHeight at a navigation cell, which is ground geometry, not scan age. Green's curve crosses the same stretch and is clear, and A* wall-time variation could also explain the difference. (b) The C6 detail is imprecise: in upper_corridor_hold the last scan was applied at the first replan_start, and body poses were also applied at replan_start in three states. (c) '3 scans and 8 poses' omits the 5 FSM odometry messages applied in the same callback. (d) The 'What it does not show' sentence at COMPONENT_RESULTS.md:217-219 is ambiguous. (e) attempt01/README.md:29-30 still calls run 02 'rerun alone'. (f) The line-ending rule in PLAN.md does not fit grid_map.cpp: that insertion has no preceding anchor and takes the ending of the line after it.

non_blocking_findings.summary: (a) Within a callback, the map's body pose (refreshed at the inner sites) can be newer than odom_pos_ (refreshed only at the timers). This is disclosed. In reference mode I confirmed that odom_pos_ drives decisions only at callback start; during planning it is only checked for finiteness. (b) Latent behaviour change: in PRESET_TARGET mode, the first odometry message calls planGlobalTrajbyGivenWps. That call now runs inside takePendingOdometry at the start of the exec timer, so the preset plan and a GEN_NEW_TRAJ step can happen in one callback. This trial uses navi_mode 3, so it is not exercised.
